item.title: Netherlands signs intent to buy Saab GlobalEye surveillance jet
item.description: The Netherlands has signed a letter of intent with Sweden to acquire a Saab GlobalEye advanced military surveillance aircraft, the Dutch government said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Netherlands has signed a letter of intent with Sweden to acquire a Saab GlobalEye advanced military surveillance aircraft, the Dutch government said on Friday. The country currently lacks its own aircraft capable of performing such tasks and has relied on NATO's aging AWACS fleet. The GlobalEye can simultaneously monitor air, sea and land over large distances and detect threats including drones and cruise missiles. Delivery of the Dutch aircraft is expected in 2031, but the Netherlands will gain access to Swedish GlobalEye aircraft from 2028 to train crews and begin operations earlier. The Dutch aircraft will join a shared pool with three Swedish GlobalEye aircraft, giving both countries' crews access to the planes. The aircraft can serve as a flying command centre and share real-time intelligence with planes, ships and ground units.

item.title: QatarEnergy seeks US LNG deals through to 2031, sources say
item.description: QatarEnergy is negotiating with several producers to secure multi-year U.S. liquefied natural gas contracts through 2031 to replace capacity knocked out by Iranian attacks that will take years to repair, three trading and industry sources said.
item.dc:creator: Marwa Rashad, Curtis Williams
item.content:encoded: QatarEnergy is negotiating with several producers to secure multi-year U.S. liquefied natural gas contracts through 2031 to replace capacity knocked out by Iranian attacks that will take years to repair, three trading and industry sources said. Discussions include with Venture Global (VG.N) , Cheniere (LNG.N) and Woodside (WDS.AX) , two of the sources said. The contract talks are part of the company's efforts to replace lost volumes from its Ras Laffan facility after two of its 14 LNG trains and a gas-to-liquids (GTL) facility were damaged by Iranian strikes in March, the sources said. The discussions also mark a shift from QatarEnergy's purchases of dozens of U.S. [USN:L8N43I294 TEXT:"spot LNG"] cargoes to help meet commitments to some of its Asian clients, suggesting it is now seeking longer-term solutions to cover the shortfall. QatarEnergy CEO Saad al-Kaabi said in March that the [USN:L6N407161 TEXT:"repairs"] would sideline 12.8 million tons per year of LNG capacity for three to five years. Having halted production in March, QatarEnergy has renewed force majeure notices monthly, most recently extending them to November, with further extensions possible as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, the sources said. QatarEnergy Trading, the trading arm of QatarEnergy that managed 10 million tons of the company's LNG portfolio, is seeking 2-3 million metric tons per annum through to 2031, one of the sources said. "They will have to buy whatever they can get their hands on," a fourth source said. QatarEnergy did not respond to a Reuters request for immediate comment. Venture Global and Cheniere declined to comment, while Woodside LNG said it does not comment on market speculation. U.S. projects under construction have a total of 25 million metric tons of LNG available for purchase, according to data compiled by research firm Rapidan Energy. Venture Global has the most LNG available with 10 mtpa uncontracted, with both Cheniere and Woodside Energy's having 6 mtpa also available for sale and 3 mtpa available from Sempra's (SRE.N) Port Arthur LNG project, the Rapidan data shows. "Qatar's current pursuit of long-term LNG volumes from other producers to help Qatar deliver into their customer contracts indicates that Qatar now sees risk to their ability to export LNG for several years," said Saul Kavonic, head of energy research and advisory at MST Marquee. "It signals that Qatar considers the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz may prove longer lasting, and the damage to Qatari LNG infrastructure has been more extensive and may take longer to repair than initially hoped," he added. About 80% of Qatar's LNG shipments are typically exported to buyers in Asia. With uncertainty about when flows would resume through the major waterway, many clients in Asia started to seek alternatives to Qatari LNG. Some market participants are stress-testing scenarios in which no Qatari gas is available, according to a fifth source.

item.title: Los legisladores de Reino Unido rechazan la propuesta de legalizar la muerte asistida
item.description: Los legisladores británicos rechazaron el viernes una propuesta para legalizar la muerte asistida de personas con enfermedades terminales, lo que supuso un importante revés para los defensores de esta causa y puso fin al último intento de modificar la ley.
item.dc:creator: Sam Tabahriti, Sarah Young
item.content:encoded: Los legisladores británicos rechazaron el viernes una propuesta para legalizar la muerte asistida de personas con enfermedades terminales, lo que supuso un importante revés para los defensores de esta causa y puso fin al último intento de modificar la ley. El resultado mantiene sin cambios la prohibición británica de la muerte asistida, lo que prolonga un debate que se remonta a décadas sobre si se debería permitir a los enfermos terminales poner fin a sus vidas con asistencia médica y cómo se podría proteger a las personas vulnerables de la coacción si se modificara la ley. La cámara baja del Parlamento, la Cámara de los Comunes, rechazó la ley por 286 votos contra 270. El proyecto de ley habría permitido a los adultos mentalmente competentes y con enfermedades terminales en Inglaterra y Gales, a los que les quedaran seis meses o menos de vida, poner fin a su vida con asistencia médica tras la aprobación de un panel de profesionales. Lauren Edwards, diputada del Partido Laborista del primer ministro Andy Burnham, había vuelto a presentar la legislación mediante un mecanismo conocido como "proyecto de ley de iniciativa parlamentaria", por el que un diputado seleccionado mediante sorteo puede intentar aprobar una ley con independencia del Gobierno. "Es un resultado enormemente decepcionante, no para mí, sino para los muchos miles de personas con enfermedades terminales y sus seres queridos a quienes se les dio esperanza cuando la Cámara de los Comunes votó a favor de este proyecto el año pasado", afirmó en un comunicado, refiriéndose a un respaldo previo a la legislación. El anterior intento de aprobar el proyecto de ley fracasó tras agotarse el plazo en la Cámara de los Lores, la cámara alta no elegida. "Dignidad en la muerte", uno de los grupos que defendía el proyecto de ley, también condenó la decisión como "un revés devastador para las personas moribundas", pero añadió que "esta cuestión no va a desaparecer. El cambio legislativo sobre la muerte asistida sigue siendo una cuestión de cuándo, no de si".

item.title: Braves place OF Lane Thomas (ribs) on injured list
item.description: The Atlanta Braves placed outfielder Lane Thomas on the 10-day injured list Friday with a strained left intercostal muscle.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Braves placed outfielder Lane Thomas on the 10-day injured list Friday with a strained left intercostal muscle. Thomas, 31, was a late scratch before Thursday's 3-1 win against the Tampa Bay Rays. His designation is retroactive to Tuesday. Acquired in a trade with the Kansas City Royals on Aug. 2, Thomas is hitting .171 with a homer and three RBIs in 21 games with Atlanta. For the season, he is batting .224 with 11 homers and 40 RBIs in 118 games with the Royals and Braves. Atlanta recalled outfielder DaShawn Keirsey Jr. from Triple-A Gwinnett in a corresponding transaction before Friday's series opener against visiting Philadelphia. The Braves enter the series with a four-game lead over the Phillies in the National League East standings. Keirsey, 29, last played in the majors with the Minnesota Twins in 2025. He is batting .247 with six homers, 36 RBIs and 40 stolen bases in 109 games at Gwinnett this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Monedas suben pese a que aumentan las expectativas de un alza de tasas de la Fed
item.description: La mayoría de las principales monedas de América Latina anotaban ganancias el viernes, pese a que un esperado dato de la inflación en Estados unidos reforzó aún más las expectativas de un alza de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal (Fed) la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Froilan Romero
item.content:encoded: La mayoría de las principales monedas de América Latina anotaban ganancias el viernes, pese a que un esperado dato de la inflación en Estados unidos reforzó aún más las expectativas de un alza de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal (Fed) la próxima semana. * El Índice de Precios al Consumo (IPC) de Estados Unidos aumentó un 0,4% el mes pasado, tras un alza del 0,1% en julio, informó el viernes la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales del Departamento de Trabajo. En los doce meses hasta agosto, la inflación al consumo se situó en el 3,4%, tras registrar el mismo incremento en julio. * Los economistas sondeados por Reuters esperaban un alza del 0,4% en términos mensuales y de un 3,4% interanual. Excluyendo los componentes volátiles de alimentos y energía, el IPC subió un 0,3% mensual, tras avanzar un 0,2% en julio. El denominado IPC subyacente fue de un 2,4% interanual en agosto, después de subir un 2,5% en julio. * Los operadores estiman ahora que hay un 85% de probabilidad de que haya una subida de un cuarto de punto en la reunión de la Fed del 15 al 16 de septiembre, frente al 70% aproximadamente que se barajaba antes del reporte. * En el ámbito geopolítico, la atención de los mercados se mantuvo en Oriente Medio, donde el conflicto entre Estados Unidos e Irán recrudeció y volvió a impulsar los precios del petróleo y, con ello, reavivó los temores por la inflación mundial. * El peso mexicano cotizaba en 16,9387 unidades por dólar, con una ganancia de 0,24% frente al precio de referencia de LSEG del jueves. Aun así, en la semana acumulaba una baja del 0,3%. * El principal índice accionario el S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, subía un 0,44%, a 64.386,28 unidades, pero se encaminaba a anotar su tercera semana consecutiva de pérdidas. * El real brasileño se apreciaba un 0,18%, a 5,0968 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice Bovespa (.BVSP) de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo retrocedía un 0,63%, a 187.088,26 puntos. * [USN:L6N4530TL TEXT:"La inflación anual de Brasil"] se moderó más de lo previsto en agosto, ya que los precios al consumidor registraron su mayor caída mensual en cuatro años, lo que refuerza los argumentos a favor de que el banco central aplique otro recorte de las tasas de interés la próxima semana. * En Argentina, el peso en el mercado mayorista de cambios operaba estable en 1.512,50 unidades por dólar para la venta. * En tanto, el índice bursátil Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires retrocedía un 0,51% debido a toma de ganancias tras las recientes mejoras. Los bonos en el segmento extrabursátil se pactaban con un alza de apenas un 0,1% promedio. * El peso chileno , caía un 0,18%, a 941,50/941,80 por dólar. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , bajaba un 0,22%, a 11.215,35 unidades. * El peso colombiano ganaba un 0,61%, a 3.071 unidades por dólar y en la bolsa el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) caía un 0,80%, a 2.605,80 puntos. * La moneda peruana, el sol , se apreciaba un 0,15%, a 3,3670/3,3690 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) subía un 0,45%, a 1.567,53 puntos. * El Banco Central de Reserva de Perú dejó el jueves estable su tasa de interés de referencia en un 4,25%, lo que extiende su pausa a un décimo tercer mes consecutivo, mientras la inflación se mantiene sobre su rango meta y los indicadores de la economía local muestran un buen desempeño.

item.title: Crypto firm Bitcoin Suisse to cut up to half of jobs in Switzerland
item.description: Bitcoin Suisse is cutting up to 60 of its 120 staff in Switzerland as it seeks to reorganise its business, the crypto firm said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bitcoin Suisse is cutting up to 60 of its 120 staff in Switzerland as it seeks to reorganise its business, the crypto firm said on Friday. "Software development and back-office capabilities will increasingly be consolidated in our international hubs, allowing us to scale faster, access broader talent pools and invest more effectively in our future offering," the Zug-based firm said. The staff reductions are due to take effect after a consultation period lasting until September 20, the company said, confirming a report by Swiss outlet Finews. Bitcoin Suisse, which was founded in 2013 and has around 200 employees globally, said it is also closing its IT development site in Copenhagen. Outside Switzerland, the company has an international hub in Bratislava and aims to establish another in Vietnam. It also has offices in Liechtenstein, Abu Dhabi and Bermuda.

item.title: India's Coforge says independent director resigns days after chairman's exit
item.description: India's Coforge said on Friday the chair of its nomination and remuneration committee, DK Singh, has resigned citing "differences and tension", days after Chairman Om Prakash Bhatt stepped down following an internal audit review.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Coforge (COFO.NS) said on Friday the chair of its nomination and remuneration committee, DK Singh, has resigned citing "differences and tension", days after Chairman Om Prakash Bhatt stepped down following an internal audit review. The resignation marks the latest escalation in a governance dispute at the IT services firm, after an internal audit found that a board evaluation report giving Bhatt a low rating was shared only with the former chair and Singh. The board had sought explanations from both Bhatt and Singh. Singh, who is also a non-executive independent director, said his resignation was "the appropriate decision" following "the unfortunate events of the past several weeks" and Bhatt's departure earlier this week, according to his September 10 letter. He said Coforge's move to a more independent board had created friction, particularly between independent and executive directors, and that new members could alter priorities in areas such as strategy, transparency and compensation. Coforge disputed Singh's claims on Friday, calling the allegation of tension "unfounded" and an "afterthought", noting there was no change in the company's direction and priorities. The company added Singh had accepted a five-year second term with the board beginning in February 2026 before the audit observations were raised. The firm also said it was "important to clarify" that Singh's resignation followed concerns identified in the internal audit review and the subsequent process of seeking explanations from both Bhatt and Singh. Singh did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Coforge's statement sent via LinkedIn and a text message. Shares of Coforge [USN:L4N45109M TEXT:"slid"] as much as 9% after Bhatt's resignation on Wednesday and saw their worst week since the week of April 20.

item.title: US declares end of largest recorded cyclosporiasis outbreak
item.description: U.S. health authorities on Friday declared the nation's largest recorded multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak over, after contaminated iceberg lettuce sickened thousands, though the FDA said it is still probing how the parasite entered the food supply.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. health authorities on Friday declared the nation's largest recorded multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak over, after contaminated iceberg lettuce sickened thousands, though the FDA said it is still probing how the parasite entered the food supply. The outbreak, which federal investigators linked to lettuce from central Mexico sourced by Taylor Farms, prompted one of the largest food recalls in recent years and renewed [USN:L6N4470WC TEXT:"scrutiny of food-safety controls"] for imported produce. It also rattled consumer confidence, with some shoppers avoiding raw fruits and vegetables as well as dining out, hurting foot traffic at restaurants such as Taco Bell (YUM.N) , Sweetgreen (SG.N) and Chipotle (CMG.N) . According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 12,883 people across 21 states fell ill after consuming contaminated lettuce. The outbreak resulted in 570 hospitalizations and two deaths, and accounted for more than half of the 19,595 laboratory-confirmed U.S. cyclosporiasis cases reported since May 1. At the peak of the outbreak, before the recall, more than 1,000 infections were reported in a single day. In August, the CDC said, infections had fallen to fewer than two per day on average. The Food and Drug Administration said on Friday it remains confident that all recalled iceberg lettuce linked to the outbreak is off the market. The CDC said best-by dates for all products linked to the outbreak have passed, and the lettuce would no longer be available in stores or restaurants. Taylor Farms [USN:L6N43J0UI TEXT:"recalled all iceberg lettuce"] sourced from central Mexico on July 17. The FDA also said it had completed on-site inspections and collected samples from lettuce farms and the processing facility in Mexico, with analysis pending, and will continue working with U.S., Mexican and state partners. Taylor Farms, retailers Walmart (WMT.O) , Target (TGT.N) , Whole Foods and restaurant chains Taco Bell (Yum Brands), Chipotle Mexican Grill and Sweetgreen did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Michigan, the state hardest hit by the outbreak, reported over 14,000 cases and [USN:L4N4401GN TEXT:"two deaths"] linked to the parasite, according to federal and state health officials. Ohio and Missouri also saw thousands of infections tied to contaminated lettuce from Taylor Farms. [USN:L4N44A1BM TEXT:"Unusually"] high case totals from Michigan were attributed to a large backlog of reports processed in August, highlighting the strain on a system [USN:L1N44W0OG TEXT:"weakened"] by federal funding cuts under the Trump administration. Before 2026, the largest U.S. cyclosporiasis season on record was reported in 2019, when roughly 4,700 illnesses were documented nationwide.

item.title: Fed rate-hike case builds as inflation fails to cool
item.description: Back-to-back hotter-than-expected inflation readings may set the table for an interest-rate hike at the Federal Reserve's meeting next week and potentially more to follow.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: Back-to-back hotter-than-expected inflation readings may disappoint the majority of U.S. central bankers who had been counting on price pressures easing on their own, setting the table for an interest-rate hike at the Federal Reserve's meeting next week and potentially more to follow. U.S. [USN:L1N452123 TEXT:"consumer price inflation"] excluding energy and food, a key measure of underlying inflation, rose 0.3% last month from the previous month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported, more than the 0.2% that economists had anticipated. From a year earlier, core CPI rose 2.4%, while overall consumer inflation measured 3.4%. Coupled with a stronger-than-expected August producer price index released on Thursday and oil prices that have soared above $100 a barrel amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, the latest data suggest inflation by the Fed's targeted measure, above the target 2% for 5-1/2 years, is again moving in the wrong direction. "Today’s clean 0.3% core CPI print, combined with the sharp rise in energy prices and persistent tensions with Iran, all but locks in a Fed rate hike next week," wrote Principal Asset Management chief global strategist Seema Shah. "After half a decade of above-target inflation, policymakers are likely to conclude that more than one hike will be needed to re-establish price stability." The Fed has left its policy rate in the 3.50%-3.75% range all year, including in a 9-3 vote in July that signaled rising sentiment inside the Fed that higher rates were already needed. Last month at the Kansas City Fed's annual gathering in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said he and his fellow central bankers may need to act if they don't have confidence that underlying inflation is moving toward 2% "clearly and at sufficient speed." Economists Friday said the August data does not appear to meet that bar. "For the Fed, it is time to put up, or shut up," Inflation Insights founder Omair Sharif wrote. "You cannot give a speech like you did at Jackson Hole and not support a rate hike at the next meeting. You will either have to back up those words or end up as the boy who cried wolf." Not all economists agree. The Fed targets 2% inflation by the 12-month change in the personal consumption expenditures price index, which weights some items, including some AI-related prices, more heavily than the CPI. Friday's CPI data showed software and accessories prices declined, and core goods prices decelerated. Pointing to those figures, Oxford Economics analysts estimate core PCE for August likely rose a "benign" 0.2%, allowing the Fed to skip a rate hike next week. But, they added, the decision is on a "knife's edge." Several other economists forecast a higher core PCE reading which they say would likely stoke concern among Warsh's colleagues who had expressed expectations that cooling inflation in June and July was the start of a welcome trend. At least two Wall Street firms now newly forecast a rate hike next week, having previously expected a hold. "This call reflects the inflation data, but also the market expectations as Chairman Warsh will want to avoid a dovish surprise next week," Piper Sandler analysts wrote. Traders of short-term interest-rate futures are now pricing about an 85% chance of a quarter-point increase at the Fed's September 15-16 meeting, versus about 70% before the report. Market pricing points to expectations for a second rate hike in December. "We don’t think today’s print portends a reacceleration of core inflation, but merely a bump on the disinflationary road," wrote Natixis economist Christopher Hodge. "We think a nudge via a hike or two is probably what the Fed will think is appropriate, starting with a hike next week."

item.title: World Cup final tug-of-war escalates as Morocco PM rebukes FA head, Spain stakes claim
item.description: The battle over who will host the 2030 World Cup final intensified on Friday after Morocco's prime minister told his country's football federation head to stop making promises before the Spanish FA chief insisted it should be held in Spain.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The battle over who will host the 2030 World Cup final intensified on Friday after Morocco's prime minister told his country's football federation head to stop making promises before the Spanish FA chief insisted it should be held in Spain. Moroccan Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch took aim at Royal Moroccan Football Federation (RMFF) President Fouzi Lekjaa, who boldly declared at a political party event that Casablanca would have the [USN:L6N4520UG TEXT:"'honour' of hosting the final"]. World soccer's governing body FIFA has not yet announced which of the three co-hosts -- Spain, Portugal or Morocco -- will host the final in 2030, with a spokesperson saying a decision would be made in due course. "Do not offer to host the big final game in Morocco while we still have not discussed the matter with our allies, Spain and Portugal. There should be some respect, brothers," Akhannouch said at a rally ahead of elections later this month. "Stop using electoral promises to pull the rug out from under us. These are huge matters. Deciding where the final will be held is a major issue." The RMFF did not respond to a request for comment on Lekjaa's remarks. SPAIN WANT WORLD CUP FINAL Spanish football federation (RFEF) head Rafael Louzan dismissed Lekjaa's promise as nothing more than election sloganeering before propping up Spain as potential hosts since they are the defending world champions. "Even though no decision has been taken (by FIFA), I believe Spain is the place because it cannot be any other way. As you know, we are currently world champions," Louzan told Cadena SER radio. "I believe Spain's organisational capacity for major events is beyond question and that is why reality dictates that the grand final cannot and must not be held anywhere other than in Spain." Reuters has contacted the RFEF for comment. As of May, Morocco's proposed 115,000-seat stadium for the 2030 World Cup was [USN:L1N42004C TEXT:"around 30% complete"], with officials overseeing the project hoping to complete construction by the end of 2027. New Jersey was selected to host the 2026 final in July and FIFA did not [USN:L1N3EO0AM TEXT:"make the announcement until February 2024"].

item.title: Germany, UAE deepen energy cooperation in agreements with RWE, SEFE
item.description: Germany and the United Arab Emirates on Friday deepened their energy ties with a number of agreements covering renewables and natural gas, part of a broader €40 billion ($46.4 billion) investment push to support industry in Europe's top economy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany and the United Arab Emirates on Friday deepened their energy ties with a number of agreements covering renewables and natural gas, part of a [USN:L1N4510K4 TEXT:"broader"] €40 billion ($46.4 billion) investment push to support industry in Europe's top economy. With a trade relationship worth around $15.5 billion a year, Germany and the UAE have been seeking closer relations amid growing political uncertainty, including the war in Iran, with energy playing a major role. RWE, Germany's largest power producer, on Friday signed a memorandum of understanding with UAE state-backed renewable energy firm Masdar over a possible joint participation in German offshore wind auctions in 2027 covering potential investment of more than €3 billion. RWE (RWEG.DE) also signed a letter of intent with ADNOC (ADNOC.UL) on future supplies of liquefied natural gas, building on an [USN:L8N3Z2148 TEXT:"initial"] framework agreement between the two parties in February. "The UAE and Germany are building on decades of trusted partnership to advance economic growth and shared prosperity for the long-term," Sultan al-Jaber, ADNOC Group CEO and the UAE's Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology, said. Both parties plan to agree terms for up to two LNG offtake agreements to supply German as well as other European and Asian markets from the early 2030s. Any LNG volumes are to come from ADNOC Gas (ADNOCGAS.AD) and ADNOC's international arm XRG. XRG, ADNOC, and German state-owned energy firm SEFE also signed an MoU to explore deeper cooperation in the fields of natural gas and LNG. Masdar and German energy infrastructure investment firm Luxcara also [USN:S8N43X05N TEXT:"agreed"] to explore joint energy storage and offshore wind investments in Germany and other markets worth more than €5 billion. ($1 = 0.8618 euros)

item.title: Se fortalecen argumentos para un alza de tasas de la Fed, porque la inflación no remite
item.description: Dos datos consecutivos de inflación superiores a lo esperado podrían decepcionar a la mayoría de las autoridades la Reserva Federal, que contaban con que las presiones sobre los precios se moderaran por sí solas, lo que allanaría el camino a una subida de las tasas de interés en su reunión de la próxima semana y, posiblemente, otras más.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: Dos datos consecutivos de inflación superiores a lo esperado podrían decepcionar a la mayoría de las autoridades la Reserva Federal, que contaban con que las presiones sobre los precios se moderaran por sí solas, lo que allanaría el camino a una subida de las tasas de interés en su reunión de la próxima semana y, posiblemente, otras más. La inflación de los precios al consumidor en Estados Unidos, excluidos la energía y los alimentos, subió un 0,3% el mes pasado respecto del mes anterior, según la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales, y más que el 0,2% que habían previsto los economistas. En comparación con el año anterior, el IPC subyacente subió un 2,4%, mientras que la inflación general de los precios al consumo se situó en el 3,4%. Junto con un índice de precios al productor de agosto más alto de lo esperado, publicado el jueves, y unos precios del petróleo que se han disparado sobre los 100 dólares el barril, en un contexto de reanudación de las hostilidades en Oriente Medio, los últimos datos sugieren que la inflación, según el indicador de referencia de la Fed, vuelve a avanzar en la dirección equivocada. "La clara cifra de hoy del IPC subyacente, del 0,3%, junto con la fuerte subida de los precios de la energía y la tensión persistente con Irán, prácticamente confirma una subida de tasas de interés de la Fed la próxima semana", escribió Seema Shah, estratega global jefe de Principal Asset Management. "Tras media década de inflación por encima del objetivo, es probable que los responsables de la política monetaria lleguen a la conclusión de que se necesitará más de una subida para restablecer la estabilidad de los precios". La Fed ha mantenido su tasa de interés oficial en el rango del 3,50% al 3,75% durante todo el año, incluso tras una votación de 9 a 3 en julio, que puso de manifiesto un creciente consenso en el seno de la Fed de que ya eran necesarias unas tasas más altas. El mes pasado, en la reunión anual de la Fed de Kansas City, el presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, dijo que él y sus colegas de los bancos centrales podrían verse obligados a actuar si no tienen la certeza de que la inflación subyacente se está acercando al 2% "de forma clara y a una velocidad suficiente". Economistas señalaron el viernes que los datos de agosto no parecen cumplir ese requisito. "Para la Fed, es hora de actuar o callarse", escribió Omair Sharif, fundador de Inflation Insights. "No se puede dar un discurso como el de Jackson Hole y luego no respaldar una subida de tasas de interés en la próxima reunión. O se respaldan esas palabras o se acaba siendo como el niño que gritó '¡lobo!'", en referencia a la fábula atribuida a Esopo. No todos los economistas están de acuerdo. La Fed se fija como objetivo una inflación del 2% según la variación interanual del índice de precios de los gastos de consumo personal (PCE), que otorga mayor peso a algunos artículos —incluidos algunos precios relacionados con la inteligencia artificial— que el IPC. Los datos del IPC del viernes mostraron que los precios del software y los accesorios descendieron, y que los precios de los bienes subyacentes se desaceleraron. Apuntando a esas cifras, analistas de Oxford Economics estiman que el PCE subyacente de agosto probablemente subió un "benigno" 0,2%, lo que permitiría a la Fed saltarse una subida de tasas de interés la próxima semana. Sin embargo, añadieron que la decisión está "en el filo de la navaja". Otros economistas pronostican una lectura más alta del PCE subyacente, lo que, según ellos, probablemente avivaría la preocupación entre los colegas de Warsh, quienes habían expresado sus expectativas de que el enfriamiento de la inflación en junio y julio fuera el inicio de una tendencia positiva. Al menos dos empresas de Wall Street prevén ahora una subida de tasas de interés la próxima semana, tras haber esperado antes que no hubiera cambios. Los operadores de futuros sobre tasas de interés a corto plazo valoran ahora en torno a un 85% la probabilidad de una subida de un cuarto de punto en la reunión de la Fed del 15 al 16 de septiembre, frente a aproximadamente el 70% antes del informe. Los precios del mercado apuntan a expectativas de una segunda subida de tasas de interés en diciembre. "No creemos que los datos de hoy auguren una reaceleración de la inflación subyacente, sino simplemente un bache en el camino desinflacionista", escribió el economista de Natixis Christopher Hodge. "Creemos que un pequeño impulso mediante una o dos subidas es probablemente lo que la Fed considerará adecuado, empezando por una subida la próxima semana".

item.title: German environmental group sues to block Rosatom-linked nuclear fuel permit
item.description: German environmental group BUND Niedersachsen has sued the state of Lower Saxony, seeking to overturn expansion of the Lingen nuclear fuel plant because it believes the involvement of Russia's Rosatom poses a security risk, it said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German environmental group BUND Niedersachsen has sued the state of Lower Saxony, seeking to overturn expansion of the Lingen nuclear fuel plant because it believes the involvement of Russia's Rosatom poses a security risk, it said on Friday. The case challenges the regional state's [USN:L8N43O20P TEXT:"clearance"] for a subsidiary of France's Framatome to produce nuclear fuel rods in the northern German town of Lingen under a licensing agreement with the state-backed Russian firm. Lower Saxony's environment ministry, with guidance from the federal environment ministry, had granted approval subject to certain conditions despite political concerns over Russia's war in Ukraine. BUND, collaborating with anti-nuclear group .ausgestrahlt, said the permit was the result of procedural errors and would pose a security risk because of Rosatom's role. In their case, brought before the regional state's upper administrative court in Lueneburg, they argue the environmental screening relied on outdated documents and that Rosatom's involvement was not fully disclosed in filings. "Because both manufacturing in Lingen and parts of quality control are carried out with machines supplied by Rosatom, production and inspection could be manipulated," BUND Germany Chair Olaf Bandt said in a statement. Berlin has said it viewed the cooperation critically, but the decision was consistent with current laws and the instrument to address the concerns would be stricter EU sanctions. The Lower Saxony environment ministry said the legal challenge would be thoroughly assessed. It also directed Reuters to a July statement by Lower Saxony's environment minister Christian Meyer, saying he was fundamentally opposed to working with Rosatom but that there had been no legal grounds for denying administrative clearance. Rosatom did not immediately reply to requests for comment. Framatome has said the collaboration was an interim step to help customers operating Russian-designed reactors diversify away from direct Russian purchases until it develops its own production technology.

item.title: Antonelli leads Spanish GP practice as Madring makes its F1 debut
item.description: Formula One championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest for Mercedes in free practice at Madrid's new Spanish Grand Prix circuit on Friday with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton close behind.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Formula One championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest for Mercedes in free practice at Madrid's new Spanish Grand Prix circuit on Friday with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton close behind. Second in a first practice led by teammate George Russell, Antonelli then set the pace in a later session halted briefly by Racing Bulls' British rookie Arvid Lindblad becoming the first F1 driver to crash at the Madring and bring out red flags. Antonelli's best lap of one minute and 33.662 seconds was 0.113 quicker than Leclerc's fastest effort. Seven-times champion Hamilton was 0.149 off the pace with Lindblad fourth despite the crash ending his session with 24 minutes to go. The 19-year-old apologised after losing control of the rear of the car and smashing into the barriers sideways at Turn 13. Russell, Antonelli's closest title rival who led practice one with a time of 1:34.077, was fifth. Leclerc and Hamilton had been third and fourth in the first session at a bright and sunny Madring, a challenging track that runs around the IFEMA exhibition centre near the capital's Barajas airport. Red Bull's four-time world champion Max Verstappen was sixth with McLaren's Oscar Piastri seventh and Racing Bulls' stand-in Yuki Tsunoda eighth and Esteban Ocon ninth for Haas. New Zealander Liam Lawson, standing in for injured French driver Isack Hadjar for the third race in a row, was 10th for Red Bull in both sessions. McLaren's reigning world champion Lando Norris missed the second session as the team changed his car's gearbox. After a [USN:L6N4530M3 TEXT:"fiery crash"] halted the earlier F2 practice, the opening Formula One session took place without interruptions or major incident. Home hero Fernando Alonso brushed the wall in his Aston Martin and was 15th and 17th in the sessions respectively, while Spain's other driver Carlos Sainz was 17th and 16th for Williams in his home city, and there were complaints from several drivers over the radio about others getting in the way. "That's just nasty," exclaimed Hulkenberg after Hamilton failed to let the German through at the final corner. Lindblad also called out Hamilton and Antonelli as "stupid" after accusing them of obstruction at the circuit's signature 'La Monumental' banked turn 12.

item.title: Candidato Flávio Bolsonaro es investigado por corrupción en el caso del Banco Master
item.description: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro, principal rival derechista del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en las elecciones del próximo mes, está siendo investigado por presuntos delitos de corrupción y blanqueo de capitales relacionados con la entidad crediticia en quiebra Banco Master, según documentos judiciales hechos públicos el viernes.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: El senador brasileño Flávio Bolsonaro, principal rival derechista del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en las elecciones del próximo mes, está siendo investigado por presuntos delitos de corrupción y blanqueo de capitales relacionados con la entidad crediticia en quiebra Banco Master, según documentos judiciales hechos públicos el viernes. La investigación sobre el senador, hijo mayor del expresidente Jair Bolsonaro, fue iniciada en julio por el magistrado de la Corte Suprema André Mendonça, nombrado por Bolsonaro y aclamado recientemente como un héroe por muchos en la derecha brasileña, incluido el propio Flávio Bolsonaro. La noticia podría agitar aún más una carrera presidencial ya de por sí volátil, en la que múltiples encuestas de opinión muestran a Flávio Bolsonaro y a Lula estadísticamente empatados en una segunda vuelta simulada. El juez abrió la investigación a petición de la policía federal como parte de una más amplia sobre el banco en quiebra. Sin embargo, los detalles de la investigación no se hicieron públicos hasta que el presidente de la Corte Suprema, Edson Fachin, ordenó el jueves por la noche que se desclasificaran los procedimientos relacionados con el caso del Banco Master. Mendónca accedió a la petición de Fachin e hizo públicas miles de páginas de expedientes judiciales. No quedó claro de inmediato cuáles eran los detalles adicionales ni las implicaciones más amplias de los documentos recién desclasificados, ya que partes del caso —incluidos los detalles de la investigación sobre el senador Bolsonaro— seguían bajo secreto de sumario mientras la policía continúa investigando activamente. Las instituciones brasileñas se han visto sacudidas por las repercusiones de la investigación, que no deja de ampliarse, y por los supuestos vínculos entre el banquero Daniel Vorcaro y funcionarios del Banco Central, altos cargos del Gobierno, políticos de la oposición y magistrados de la Corte Suprema. INVESTIGACIÓN TIENE ORIGEN EN UNA PELÍCULA La investigación sobre Flávio Bolsonaro se deriva de las dudas sobre una inversión que supuestamente solicitó a Vorcaro, propietario del Banco Master, para ayudar a financiar "Dark Horse", una película sobre su padre protagonizada por el actor estadounidense Jim Caviezel. Las dudas sobre la financiación de la película surgieron en mayo, lo que llevó al senador a reconocer que había solicitado apoyo financiero a Vorcaro, aunque negó haber cometido ninguna irregularidad. Las revelaciones le costaron apoyo en las encuestas de opinión de aquel momento. Los documentos desclasificados muestran que la policía federal solicitó entonces una investigación, autorizada por el juez Mendonça, para examinar si el senador Bolsonaro había cometido delitos de blanqueo de capitales, cambio de divisas ilícito y corrupción. La policía citó las donaciones realizadas por Vorcaro, que fue detenido en marzo, a la película como motivo para solicitar la investigación. El senador ha afirmado en repetidas ocasiones que sus relaciones con el banquero eran estrictamente privadas y no guardaban relación con los asuntos investigados por la policía federal. CRISIS EN LA CORTE SUPREMA Estos nuevos acontecimientos intensifican una crisis que sacude a Brasil, mientras los votantes se adentran en una campaña electoral inusualmente reñida en la que cualquier acontecimiento importante podría inclinar la balanza a favor del candidato de izquierda Lula o de Bolsonaro. Fachin ha intentado resolver un enfrentamiento público entre los magistrados Mendonça y Alexandre de Moraes —quien también ha sido mencionado en la investigación sobre el Banco Master—, que ha sumido a la Corte en una de sus crisis internas más graves de las últimas décadas. Mendonça hizo públicos a principios de este mes documentos de la investigación, entre ellos docenas de mensajes que, según la policía, Vorcaro envió a Moraes. Las revelaciones provocaron peticiones para que se lleve a cabo una investigación sin precedentes a un magistrado de la Corte Suprema en activo, por acusaciones de que Moraes actuó como asesor del banquero. Moraes, en respuesta, acusó a Mendonca de abusar de su autoridad. Fachin convocó una sesión plenaria para el martes, en la que se espera que los diez miembros de la Corte debatan las acusaciones relativas a la relación de Moraes con Vorcaro. Los partidarios del senador Bolsonaro han intentado vincular a Lula con Moraes, quien persiguió al expresidente Bolsonaro por un complot golpista de 2023 y logró su condena el año pasado. Durante las concentraciones del Día de la Independencia celebradas el lunes en São Paulo, un globo hinchable gigante con la imagen de Mendonça se elevaba sobre la multitud reunida para apoyar la campaña de Bolsonaro. En un intento por distanciarse de la crisis en la Corte, Lula apoyó públicamente que se haga pública la investigación horas antes de la decisión de Fachin. "Siempre que haya una acusación que implique al poder judicial o a la política, debe hacerse pública para que todo el mundo sepa lo que está pasando", dijo el jueves en una entrevista con la cadena SBT. "Que se investigue todo, que se revele todo, independientemente de a quién perjudique".

item.title: US consumer inflation picks up in August
item.description: U.S. consumer prices accelerated in August, while a key measure of underlying inflation posted its largest increase in four months, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: U.S. consumer prices accelerated in August, while a key measure of underlying inflation posted its largest increase in four months, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week. The Labor Department's Consumer Price Index report on Friday followed strong readings in several components of the [USN:L1N4500SJ TEXT:"Producer Price Index"] released on Thursday that feed into the Personal Consumption Expenditures price indexes, the inflation measures the U.S. central bank tracks for its 2% target. Soon after the CPI data was published, financial markets priced in a roughly 91% chance of a rate hike next week, up from about 72% on Thursday, CME's FedWatch tool showed. "It wasn't as hot as yesterday's PPI, but today's CPI left the Fed with less room to maneuver as it tries to maintain its inflation-fighting credentials," said Ellen Zentner, chief economic strategist at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management. The Consumer Price Index increased 0.4% last month after edging up 0.1% in July, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. In the 12 months through August, consumer inflation advanced 3.4% after rising by the same margin in July. The rise in the CPI was in line with economists' expectations. A 3.9% jump in gasoline prices after two straight monthly declines accounted for more than a third of the increase in the CPI over the month. Other motor fuels, which include diesel, surged 9.6%. [USN:L4N45202S TEXT:"Oil prices"] have climbed back above $100 a barrel, while diesel prices are at record highs, suggesting inflation was set to remain elevated and broaden out in the coming months. There was some respite for consumers at the supermarket. Food prices edged up 0.1% for a second straight month. Grocery prices were unchanged amid muted increases in the prices of meat and fish. Fruit and vegetable prices fell 0.4% over the month, weighed down by a 6.2% drop in the cost of lettuce because of a Cyclospora outbreak. But egg prices increased 2.9%, while nonalcoholic beverages cost more as did dairy and related products. With diesel prices at a record high, consumers could soon face higher prices at the supermarket as nearly all the goods are transported by road, economists warned. Some saw price pressures persisting because of tariffs on imports, most recently against Canada, one of the United States' top trade partners. Frustration over higher prices, especially for gasoline and food, has led to a sharp erosion in President [USN:L6N44S0Y9 TEXT:"Donald Trump's"] approval ratings and could cost his Republican party control of the U.S. Congress in the November midterm elections. CORE INFLATION HIGHER OVER THE MONTH Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI rose 0.3% last month, the largest increase since April. That was above economists' expectations for a second straight month of a 0.2% gain. The so-called core CPI increased 2.4% year-on-year in August after rising 2.5% in July. Core CPI inflation was over the month driven by a 2.7% increase in airline fares amid rising jet fuel costs. There were also solid increases in the prices of education, communication as well as used cars and trucks. Rents rose 0.2% while the cost of hotel and motel rooms rebounded 2.4%. But healthcare costs eased while prices for prescription medication were unchanged. The cost of motor vehicle insurance fell 0.8% while apparel prices were unchanged. With the CPI and PPI data in hand, economists' estimates for August's core PCE price index converged around a 0.28% increase, which would round up to 0.3%. Core PCE inflation rose 0.2% in July. Estimates for the year-on-year increase in core PCE inflation ranged from 3.2% to 3.3%. Core PCE inflation advanced 3.3% in the 12 months through July. The August PCE inflation report will include changes to the methodology, which some economists say could lower the core inflation rate by a couple of basis points. The Fed's benchmark overnight interest rate is currently in a 3.50%-3.75% range. The dollar was little changed against a basket of currencies. U.S. Treasury yields initially rose after the inflation data before pulling back. The odds of a rate increase had diminished following comments by Fed Governor [USN:S0N4490CF TEXT:"Christopher Waller"] at a Reuters NEXT Newsmaker event last week that he was inclined to argue in favor of keeping rates steady if data confirmed inflation pressures were cooling. Fed Chairman [USN:L6N44N17B TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] last month said the central bank will "have work to do" if policymakers don't get the confidence they need that inflation is heading down to 2%. But Trump is pressuring the Fed to cut rates, posting on social media last week "LOWER THE RATE OR I'LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT." Economists have blamed what they called political intimidation for the surge in yields on long-term U.S. government bonds. Some expected the Fed to tighten policy next Wednesday to underscore its independence.

item.title: Recruiter SThree rejects US-based Circle8's takeover bid
item.description: Recruiter SThree unanimously rejected an unsolicited all-cash takeover approach from U.S.-based Circle8 Group on Friday, saying the proposal significantly undervalues the British company and its future prospects.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Recruiter SThree (STEMS.L) unanimously rejected an unsolicited all-cash takeover approach from U.S.-based Circle8 Group (CIRC.O) on Friday, saying the proposal significantly undervalues the British company and its future prospects. Here are some details: SThree, which has a market value of £336 million ($453.77 million), said it remains confident in long-term growth prospects for the business. Shares in the London-listed firm were down 3.7%. Under the U.K. Takeover Code, Circle8 must either announce a firm intention to make an offer or walk away by October 7. British [USN:L4N43G0HA TEXT:"recruiters"] have been leaning on cost cuts to shore up profits as AI-driven efficiencies weigh on hiring, with firms also increasingly shifting toward shorter-term contracts. In July, SThree's half-year like-for-like pretax profit [USN:L4N43N0CF TEXT:"fell"] by three-quarters, as an AI-driven hiring slowdown and the economic impact of the Iran war weighed. Technology and workforce solutions firm Circle8 [USN:TUA6Q8RZ0 TEXT:"said"] on Thursday its Nasdaq valuation undervalues its potential and the proposed deal would create a nearly $3 billion revenue platform. Circle8 did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. ($1 = 0.7405 pounds)

item.title: Mendonça abriu inquérito contra Flávio por corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão em caso "Dark Horse"
item.description: O ministro André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou em julho a abertura de inquérito para investigar o candidato a presidente e senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) por supostos crimes de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas no caso dos repasses feitos pelo banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, para financiar o filme "Dark Horse", a cinebiografia sobre o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, segundo decisão tornada pública nesta sexta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito, Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: O ministro André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou em julho a abertura de inquérito para investigar o candidato a presidente e senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) por supostos crimes de corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas no caso dos repasses feitos pelo banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, para financiar o filme "Dark Horse", a cinebiografia sobre o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, segundo decisão tornada pública nesta sexta-feira. A determinação de Mendonça, revelada na íntegra com a derrubada do sigilo das apurações do Banco Master atendendo a pedido do presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, foi requerida pela Polícia Federal, que defendia o aprofundamento das investigações, e teve o aval da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR). "Nessa perspectiva, considerando os termos da representação da Polícia Federal e a concordância da Procuradoria-Geral da República, autorizo... a instauração de procedimento investigatório... para apuração da hipótese criminal delineada pela autoridade policial", disse Mendonça, em despacho de duas páginas. Ao comentar a divulgação da abertura de inquérito durante evento de campanha em Manaus, Flávio disse estar tranquilo e afirmou que ficará comprovado que o patrocínio de Vorcaro ao filme foi uma "relação privada". “Estão requentando uma decisão desde julho, no momento quando ultrapassamos em todas as pesquisas o ‘Império do Mal’. Estamos numa eleição presidencial e não é novidade para ninguém que vão tentar fazer de tudo para desestabilizar e inventar coisas onde não tem”, afirmou o senador. “Sempre disse que a relação com o filme foi privada, um patrocínio privado em relação ao filme do presidente Bolsonaro. É muito positivo para confirmar o que sempre falei.” Os detalhes dessa investigação aberta em julho não são de conhecimento público porque o caso segue sob sigilo. Na época da abertura de inquérito, em julho, a Reuters havia noticiado a determinação de Mendonça, mas não tinha detalhes das alegações para a investigação contra o presidenciável. A representação de 16 páginas da PF do dia 8 de julho, tornada pública nesta sexta-feira, detalha os indícios de participação de Flávio Bolsonaro na "viabilização e cobrança dos aportes" a Daniel Vorcaro para financiamento da produção do filme. O documento relata uma série de tratativas entre o senador e o banqueiro e pessoas ligadas a ele desde ao menos dezembro de 2024 até 16 de novembro de 2025, às vésperas da primeira fase da Operação Compliance Zero, que levou à prisão pela primeira vez de Vorcaro. Nessa ocasião, Flávio Bolsonaro tentou contato com Vorcaro e, posteriormente, encaminhou mensagem afirmando: “Irmão, estou e estarei contigo sempre, não tem meia conversa entre a gente. Só preciso que me dê uma luz! Abs!”, segundo degravação de áudio citada na representação. "Tais elementos indicam que o senador Flávio Nantes Bolsonaro não aparece apenas como terceiro mencionado em comunicações de outras pessoas, mas como interlocutor direto de Daniel Vorcaro em tratativas relacionadas ao financiamento da produção, inclusive com cobranças de pagamentos, reuniões presenciais e acompanhamento do andamento das gravações", disse a PF na representação. O caso do apoio de Vorcaro a Flávio sobre o filme foi revelado em reportagem em maio do site Intercept Brasil. O documento da PF informa que foi localizado nas comunicações extraídas do aparelho celular de Vorcaro um contrato que previa "investimento total de US$24.000.000,00, correspondente, à época, a aproximadamente R$ 134 milhões" -- confirmando dados reportados pelo Intercept Brasil. Segundo a PF, a dinâmica recomenda o aprofundamento das investigações para esclarecer, entre outras questões, a origem dos recursos destinados a financiar o filme, a utilização de empresas como intermediárias dos pagamentos, beneficiários finais dos valores remetidos ao exterior, e o papel efetivamente exercido por Flávio Bolsonaro e outras sete pessoas na "estruturação, cobrança, execução e destinação dos aportes". Uma outra linha sob investigação, segundo fontes da PF, é se parte dos recursos para financiar o filme teria sido desviada e usada para bancar a estadia do ex-deputado Eduardo Bolsonaro, irmão de Flávio e filho de Jair Bolsonaro nos Estados Unidos. O procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, se manifestou a favor do pedido da PF de abertura de inquérito e realização de diligências, além de defender a análise de eventuais propostas legislativas apresentadas por Flávio Bolsonaro que poderiam ser de interesse do Banco Master e de empresas ligadas a Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Brazil presidential hopeful Bolsonaro under investigation over alleged corruption, court document shows
item.description: Brazil's Supreme Court opened an investigation in July into Senator Flavio Bolsonaro over alleged corruption and money laundering crimes as part of a broader probe into failed lender Banco Master, according to a court document unsealed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazil's Supreme Court opened an investigation in July into Senator Flavio Bolsonaro over alleged corruption and money laundering crimes as part of a broader probe into failed lender Banco Master, according to a [USN:L1N4530BQ TEXT:"court document unsealed"] on Friday. The eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro is the leading right-wing challenger to leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in next month's election. The investigation into Flavio Bolsonaro was opened by Justice Andre Mendonca following a request from Brazil's Federal Police, which pointed to donations made by Banco Master's former chief executive Daniel Vorcaro to a movie about the senator's father.

item.title: Brazil election challenger Bolsonaro under investigation over alleged corruption in Banco Master case
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the leading right-wing challenger to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in next month's election, is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering tied to failed lender Banco Master, according to court documents unsealed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the leading right-wing challenger to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in next month's election, is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering tied to failed lender [USN:L6N3ZZ1EP TEXT:"Banco Master"], according to court documents unsealed on Friday. The probe into the senator, the eldest son of former right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro, was opened in July by Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca, a Bolsonaro appointee who has recently been [USN:L6N450133 TEXT:"hailed as a hero"] by many on Brazil's right, including Flavio Bolsonaro himself. The development could further shake an already volatile presidential race, with multiple opinion polls showing Flavio Bolsonaro and Lula statistically tied in a simulated second-round runoff. The judge opened the probe at the request of federal police as part of a broader investigation into the failed bank. But details of the investigation only became public after Chief Justice Edson Fachin ordered the proceedings related to the Banco Master case unsealed late on Thursday. Mendonca complied with Fachin's request, releasing thousands of pages of court records. Further details and the broader implications of the newly unsealed documents were not immediately clear, as parts of the case, including details of the investigation into Senator Bolsonaro, remained under secrecy as police actively investigate. Brazil's institutions have been shaken by the fallout from the expanding probe and alleged ties between banker Daniel Vorcaro and [USN:L1N3ZS17G TEXT:"central bank officials"], senior government members, opposition politicians and Supreme Court justices. PROBE STEMS FROM FILM FINANCING The investigation into Flavio Bolsonaro stems from questions over an investment he allegedly solicited from Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to help finance "Dark Horse," a film about his father that stars [USN:L6N41R15D TEXT:"U.S. actor Jim Caviezel"]. Questions about the film's financing emerged [USN:L1N41S0H7 TEXT:"in May"], prompting the senator to acknowledge seeking financial backing from Vorcaro, while denying wrongdoing. The disclosures cost him support in opinion polls at the time. The unsealed documents show the federal police then requested an investigation, authorized by Justice Mendonca, to examine whether Senator Bolsonaro committed money laundering, illicit foreign exchange and corruption. The unsealed police report confirms much of a report by news website The Intercept Brasil from May that first detailed communications between the senator and Vorcaro up until the banker's first arrest in November 2025. "Brother, I am and always will be with you," Bolsonaro told the disgraced banker in an audio message at the time, according to the report. Police said data extracted from Vorcaro's cellphone showed he transferred about $12 million in 2025 to a U.S.-based fund linked to former lawmaker Eduardo Bolsonaro, the senator's brother, who now lives in Texas, as part of efforts to finance the film. One screenshot included in the documents suggests Eduardo Bolsonaro advised Vorcaro's team on the management of the funds in the United States. Investigators are seeking to determine the origin of the money, the companies used to channel it, and its ultimate beneficiaries. Flavio Bolsonaro did not immediately reply to a request for comment. But he and his brother have always denied wrongdoing. SUPREME COURT CRISIS The new developments intensify a crisis rattling Brazil as voters head into an [USN:L1N4520VL TEXT:"unusually tight election campaign"] in which any major development could tip the balance in favor of either left-wing Lula or Bolsonaro. Fachin has sought to [USN:L1N4510HK TEXT:"resolve a public clash"] between justices Mendonca and Alexandre de Moraes, who has also been mentioned in the Banco Master probe, that thrust the court into one of its [USN:L6N44U1B6 TEXT:"most severe internal crises"] in decades. Mendonca made public documents from the investigation earlier this month, including dozens of messages that police say Vorcaro sent to Moraes. The disclosures prompted calls for an unprecedented investigation into a sitting Supreme Court justice over allegations that Moraes acted as an adviser to the banker. Moraes, in response, accused Mendonca of abusing his authority. Fachin scheduled a full-court session for Tuesday, when the court's 10-member bench is expected to discuss allegations regarding Moraes' relationship with Vorcaro. 'DISCLOSE EVERYTHING,' SAYS LULA Senator Bolsonaro's supporters have [USN:L1N44Z0II TEXT:"attempted to link Lula to Moraes"], who pursued former President Bolsonaro over a 2023 coup plot and [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"secured his conviction"] last year. During Independence Day rallies in Sao Paulo on Monday, a giant inflatable balloon depicting Mendonca towered over crowds gathered to support Bolsonaro's campaign. Seeking to distance himself from the crisis at the court, Lula publicly supported unsealing the investigation hours before Fachin's decision. "Whenever there is an allegation involving the judiciary or politics, it should be made public so everyone knows what is happening," he said in an interview with SBT TV on Thursday. "Investigate everything, disclose everything, regardless of who it hurts."

item.title: Canal+ and LaLiga sign anti-piracy pact spanning nearly 50 countries
item.description: French streamer Canal+ and Spanish football league LaLiga said on Friday they had signed an anti-piracy agreement spanning nearly 50 countries, joining forces to combat illegal streaming.
item.dc:creator: Basile Day, Leo Marchandon
item.content:encoded: French streamer Canal+ (CAN.L) and Spanish football league LaLiga said on Friday they had signed an anti-piracy agreement spanning nearly 50 countries, joining forces to combat illegal streaming. The partnership, covering markets in Europe, sub-Saharan Africa and Haiti where Canal+ broadcasts LaLiga, will combine the companies' anti-piracy technology and include joint investigations and lobbying work. Financial terms were not disclosed. "The immediate next step is to bring our teams together and have them work jointly," Canal+ Chief Executive Maxime Saada told Reuters. LaLiga President Javier Tebas said the deal had been months in the making and was aimed at improving the response to criminal networks that change tactics quickly. "Piracy does affect the clubs' fundamental income source: audiovisual rights," Tebas said. Broadcast income at Spanish professional clubs fell 5.2% to 1.43 billion euros ($1.66 billion) in 2024/25, while commercial revenue rose to 1.58 billion euros, overtaking broadcasting as the largest source of income, according to LaLiga. "In virtually every rights negotiation around the world, piracy is raised," Tebas said. "Many rights holders have to do much more." Saada said piracy in France was estimated to wipe out 1.5 billion euros in value and cost the state several hundred million euros in tax revenue each year. Tebas said sophisticated networks were involved in piracy operations, citing China-based companies that mixed legal and illegal activities as an example of how complex structures allowed operators to evade laws. ($1 = 0.8626 euros)

item.title: Sweden's fractured left holds slim lead in polls before Sunday election
item.description: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc holds a narrow lead ahead of Sunday's parliamentary election, three opinion polls showed on Friday, two days before what is seen as a referendum on the incumbent right-wing government's alliance with the far-right.
item.dc:creator: Ilze Filks, Terje Solsvik
item.content:encoded: Sweden's centre-left opposition bloc holds a narrow lead ahead of Sunday's [USN:L8N4510ME TEXT:"parliamentary election"], three opinion polls showed on Friday, two days before what is seen as a referendum on the incumbent right-wing government's alliance with the far-right. Across Europe, far-right parties have been on the rise, with Alternative for Germany, which opposes immigration and backs closer ties with Russia, [USN:L1N44Z08Z TEXT:"winning a state election"] and Marine Le Pen [USN:L8N44W148 TEXT:"leading polls"] for next year's presidential vote in France. In Sweden, Social Democrats leader [USN:L8N44Z0WO TEXT:"Magdalena Andersson"] narrowly remains favourite to become prime minister again after four years in opposition and replace [USN:L8N4511E2 TEXT:"Ulf Kristersson"] of the centre-right Moderates. Sweden's four left-leaning parties between them have support of between 49.3% and 50.8%, giving them from 175 to 180 seats in the 349-seat parliament, according to the surveys conducted by the Ipsos, Demoskop and Indikator Opinion polling firms. Backing for the coalition government and its far-right support party, the Sweden Democrats, stands at 47.6% to 49.0%, corresponding to between 169 and 174 seats, the polls released by Swedish Radio and dailies Aftonbladet and DN showed. Kristersson has overseen a shift in Sweden away from the liberalism for which the country was once known, introducing some of Europe's toughest policies on [USN:L8N44Z0EO TEXT:"immigration"]. Andersson's bloc, which has pledged higher public spending, has retained a majority in every poll published this year, with most of the recent surveys pointing to a winning margin of around 10 seats. But one of the surveys on Friday showed a margin of a single seat, mirroring Sweden's close-fought election of 2022. In mid-August, the centre-left held a 10 percentage point lead in several polls, which political scientists at the time said was a [USN:L8N44F097 TEXT:"nearly insurmountable gap"] to bridge before election day. Kristersson says that if his bloc wins, the [USN:L8N43F0IH TEXT:"Sweden Democrats"], which has apologised for its past links with [USN:L8N4511E2 TEXT:"neo-Nazism"], would [USN:L1N40K0GO TEXT:"join the government"] for the first time. DIVIDED LEFT The centre-left remains divided over which parties should be included in a government headed by the Social Democrats, with the Centre Party and the Left Party each ruling out taking part if the other is in. The parties also differ on key policies, from a tax on billionaires to whether Sweden should build new nuclear reactors. This may in turn lead to lengthy negotiations and the formation of a minority government including some, but not all, opposition parties if the left wins. The rival blocs both support Ukraine in its fight against Russia's invasion as well as military rearmament at home and relief for households hit by the rising [USN:L8N44T0FS TEXT:"cost of living"]. But while the campaign focused on a range of issues including Sweden's welfare state, immigration and crime, there was no single dominant issue, experts said. "Nothing has really stuck, it's been sort of unsatisfactory in that sense," said Nicholas Aylott, an associate professor at Sodertorn University. The Social Democrats remain Sweden's biggest single party with support between 27.4% and 29.7%, down from 30.3% in the 2022 vote, the polls show. The anti-immigration [USN:L1N43O0G2 TEXT:"Sweden Democrats party"] maintained its position as the governing bloc's biggest group with 18.3% to 19.0% support, down from 20.5% since the 2022 election, the polls showed. The party has been propping up the ruling coalition without being part of the cabinet.

item.title: Após pedido de Fachin, Mendonça retira sigilo de investigações sobre Master
item.description: O ministro André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), retirou os sigilos de parte dos inquéritos sobre o Banco Master, após um pedido neste sentido do presidente do Supremo, Edson Fachin, conforme decisão do magistrado divulgada na noite de quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O ministro André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), retirou os sigilos de parte dos inquéritos sobre o Banco Master, após um pedido neste sentido do presidente do Supremo, Edson Fachin, conforme decisão do magistrado divulgada na noite de quinta-feira. A retirada do sigilo vem ao fim de uma semana de forte agravamento da crise no STF envolvendo desdobramentos das investigações em torno do Master, e dias antes de sessão plenária, marcada por Fachin para a próxima terça-feira, para tratar da controvérsia em torno de relatório da Polícia Federal que apontou vínculos de Daniel Vorcaro, dono do Master, com o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, entre outras questões. Em seu pedido, Fachin pediu a Mendonça que retirasse os sigilos envolvendo o Master, exceto "o que diga respeito a diligências cujo sigilo seja imprescindível à realização da medida". Em resposta, Mendonça levantou o sigilo do procedimento principal sobre o Master e de 14 outros procedimentos relacionados a ele. Na quinta-feira, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defendeu a retirada do sigilo de todas as investigações envolvendo o Master e criticou o que chamou de vazamentos seletivos que visam influenciar o processo eleitoral. O levantamento do sigilo tem potencial de revelar detalhes das investigações que podem impactar a eleição presidencial de outubro, na qual Lula busca a reeleição e tem como principal adversário o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). Entre os pontos da investigação que podem ser detalhados estão as relações de Vorcaro com servidores do BC, que teriam atuado para beneficiar o Master dentro da autarquia; contratos milionários que o Master fez com o escritório de advocacia da esposa de Moraes e as relações de Flávio com Vorcaro envolvendo pedido de dinheiro para a realização do filme "Dark Horse", sobre a vida do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, atualmente em prisão domiciliar após ser condenado por tentativa de golpe de Estado. A retirada do sigilo de investigações envolvendo o Master vem em meio à escalada de uma crise no Supremo que tem como atores principais Mendonça e Moraes. Após a divulgação do relatório da PF vinculando Moraes a Vorcaro, Moraes pediu abertura de investigação contra Mendonça por abuso de autoridade e crime de responsabilidade, apontando que o colega teria direcionado investigações contra ele. Na terça-feira, em mais uma escalada da crise, Mendonça determinou o [USN:L1N4500FG TEXT:"afastamento"] do diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, e do diretor de inteligência da corporação, Leandro Almada, apontando que a PF o teria monitorado de forma ilegal, assim como o ministro da Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU), Jorge Messias. Relatórios de inteligência apócrifos serviram de base para Moraes pedir a investigação de Mendonça. No dia seguinte, entretanto, em resposta a um recurso de Rodrigues impetrado em outro procedimento, o ministro Flávio Dino [USN:L1N4510HB TEXT:"reintegrou"] o diretor-geral da PF e Almada aos seus cargos, em uma decisão recheada de recados a Mendonça. Diante do agravamento da crise, Fachin [USN:L1N45116L TEXT:"decidiu agir"] e suspendeu tanto a decisão de Mendonça, que afastou Rodrigues, quanto a de Dino, que o reintegrou ao cargo, e manteve o chefe da PF no posto. O presidente do Supremo também retirou Moraes da relatoria do inquérito das fake news. Fachin determinou ainda a suspensão do caso relatado por Mendonça em que foi produzido um relatório da PF que apontou vínculos do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro com Moraes, Andrei Rodrigues, e o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet. O presidente do STF disse que o plenário deve analisar o caso -- e outras questões -- de forma extraordinária na próxima terça-feira, dia 15 de setembro.

item.title: China AI developer Z.AI launches $5 billion Hong Kong share, convertible bond sales, term sheet shows
item.description: Beijing-based artificial intelligence company Z.AI Co Ltd has launched a Hong Kong share placement of about $2 billion and a concurrent convertible bond sale of about $3 billion, according to term sheets seen by Reuters on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Beijing-based artificial intelligence company Z.AI Co Ltd (2513.HK) has launched a Hong Kong share placement of about $2 billion and a concurrent convertible bond sale of about $3 billion, according to term sheets seen by Reuters on Friday. The fundraising comes as Chinese AI developers [USN:L4N43A1D1 TEXT:"seek capital"] for the costly computing infrastructure and talent needed to [USN:L1N44B0F2 TEXT:"compete"] with larger U.S. rivals. Z.AI, formerly known as Zhipu AI, [USN:L1N3Y902D TEXT:"went public"] in Hong Kong in January and [USN:L4N43A12V TEXT:"raised"] about $4 billion in a follow-on share sale in July. Rival MiniMax (0100.HK) also [USN:L1N3YA01E TEXT:"listed"] in Hong Kong earlier this year, while [USN:L1N44V07O TEXT:"Moonshot"] and [USN:L4N4500M5 TEXT:"DeepSeek"] are pursuing potential listings in Hong Kong and Shanghai, respectively, Reuters has reported. Z.AI is offering 21.97 million new Hong Kong shares at HK$714 ($91.05) each, a 10% discount to Friday's closing price of HK$793, according to the sheet. The company is also selling 20.14 billion yuan ($3 billion) of zero-coupon bonds due in September 2027, the sheet showed. The yuan-denominated bonds will be settled in U.S. dollars. The bonds will be issued at 100% to 100.5% of their face value, giving a yield ranging from negative 0.5% to zero, according to the sheet. The initial conversion price is HK$892.50, a 25% premium to the HK$714 share placement price. Z.AI can redeem all, but not part, of the bonds from February 18, 2027, if its shares trade at or above 130% of the conversion price for 20 out of 30 trading days, according to the sheet. The company plans to use proceeds from both deals for research and development, computing resources and related infrastructure, according to the sheet. They will also fund expansion, strategic investments, potential acquisitions, working capital and other corporate purposes, the sheet showed. The share placement and bond sale are being conducted at the same time but are not dependent on each other closing. CICC is sole global coordinator and joint bookrunner with Guotai Junan Securities (Hong Kong) on the fundraising. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent outside office hours. ($1 = 7.8421 Hong Kong dollars) ($1 = 6.7080 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.content:encoded: Los precios del cobre anotaron su primera caída semanal desde junio a pesar de que se estabilizaron el viernes tras una fuerte caída en la sesión anterior, después de que Reuters informó de que la Casa Blanca aún no había tomado una decisión sobre la imposición de aranceles a este metal. * El cobre a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres operaba estable en 14.238 dólares por tonelada métrica a las 1600 GMT. El jueves cayó un 3,6% tras alcanzar un máximo histórico de 14.875 dólares y va camino de cerrar la semana con un descenso del 1,2%, lo que pondría fin a una racha alcista de diez semanas. * "El mercado se ha visto atrapado en posiciones largas", dijo Alastair Munro, estratega sénior de metales básicos de Marex, en un correo electrónico. * "Las existencias de cobre siguen siendo escasas a nivel geográfico y mover cantidades significativas de dinero debería llevar algún tiempo", añadió. "Por lo tanto, vemos potencial para una mayor escasez en los próximos meses, pero en este momento lo más importante es la gestión del riesgo". * Las existencias disponibles de cobre en la LME se mantuvieron estables en 117.600 toneladas, pero en China las existencias de la Bolsa de Futuros de Shanghái cayeron por segunda semana consecutiva, desplomándose un 13%, a 54.780 toneladas, su nivel más bajo desde enero de 2024. * Las existencias en la bolsa estadounidense COMEX siguieron aumentando lentamente a pesar de la caída de la prima del cobre en Estados Unidos. * El diferencial del cobre a tres meses de la LME pasó a situarse en "contango" el jueves, una estructura de mercado en la que los precios de los futuros son más altos que los de la entrega inmediata, lo que apunta a una disminución de las preocupaciones sobre la disponibilidad a corto plazo. * El contrato al contado cotizaba por última vez con un descuento de 4,50 dólares por tonelada respecto al contrato a tres meses. * El resto del complejo de la LME se situó en números rojos, ya que el aumento de los costos de financiamiento y los temores inflacionarios agitaron los mercados. El aluminio cayó un 1,1%, a 3.257,50 dólares por tonelada; el zinc bajó un 0,5%, a 3.874,50 dólares y el plomo también perdió un 0,5%, a 1.891,50 dólares. * Por su parte, el níquel cedió un 1,2%, a 16.465 dólares, tocando su mínimo de dos meses, mientras que el estaño cayó un 2%, a 53.255 dólares, alcanzando su nivel más bajo desde el 28 de julio.

item.title: Oro sube en medio de apuestas de alza de tasas de la Fed tras dato de inflación EEUU
item.description: Los precios del oro subieron más de un 1% el viernes, recuperándose de pérdidas recientes y encontrando un suelo a corto plazo, pese a sólidos datos de inflación de Estados Unidos que reforzaron las expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal la próxima semana.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: Los precios del oro subieron más de un 1% el viernes, recuperándose de pérdidas recientes y encontrando un suelo a corto plazo, pese a sólidos datos de inflación de Estados Unidos que reforzaron las expectativas de un alza de tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal la próxima semana. * El oro al contado ganó un 1,2%, a 4.366,69 dólares por onza, a las 1522 GMT, pero cayó un 1,4% en la semana. * "El oro se está recuperando rápidamente tras un breve bajón, ya que los datos del IPC podrían estar consolidando las expectativas de un alza de tasas de la Fed. La volatilidad es moderada, ya que el mercado tenía descontada una subida en un 70%", afirmó Tai Wong, operador independiente. * "La evolución de los precios sugiere que el oro está encontrando un suelo a corto plazo tras el reciente retroceso", agregó. * Los futuros del oro en Estados Unidos mejoraban un 0,1%, a 4.409,3 dólares. * Los precios cayeron casi un 2% el jueves, tras un informe de precios al productor (IPP) en Estados Unidos que mostró un aumento en línea con las expectativas en agosto. * El índice de precios al consumo (IPC) subió un 0,4 % el mes pasado, tras registrar un leve incremento del 0,1% en julio, según informó el viernes la Oficina de Estadísticas Laborales del Departamento de Trabajo. * Entre otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado subió un 1,4%, a 64,43 dólares por onza, pero cayó un 2,6% en la semana; el platino ganó un 0,9%, a 1.793,16 dólares; y el paladio sumó un 2,5%, a 1.313,5 dólares. Estos dos últimos metales declinaron en la semana.

item.title: TSX rises as easing oil prices offset Fed rate hike concerns
